Real vs. Synthetic Feature Distribution Overlays
Real vs. Synthetic Feature Distribution Overlays involves plotting overlapping feature histograms comparing real dataset samples against generated synthetic samples to evaluate distribution match.

High-Dimensional Data Points
High-dimensional data points are complex data entities existing in multiple dimensions, requiring techniques to reduce dimensions for easier analysis.

2D or 3D Coordinate Space
2D or 3D coordinate space represents simplified data visualization, with two or three dimensions instead of the high-dimensional data points.

PCA
Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used for reducing the dimensionality of high-dimensional data while retaining most of the variance in the data.

t-SNE
t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) is a method used for visualizing high-dimensional data in 2D or 3D, focusing on local structure rather than global variance.

Latent Space
Latent space refers to the space in which hidden or abstract features of the data are represented, allowing for interpolation and visualization of latent variables.<SEP>Latent space refers to the abstract space used by generative models for representing the parameters of a probability distribution.

Latent Vectors
Latent vectors are abstract data points representing hidden or latent features in high-dimensional data spaces.

Random Latent Vectors
Random latent vectors are used in interpolation methods like Latent Space Interpolation Trajectories to generate and verify smooth transformations in latent space.

Ian Goodfellow

Stability

Saturation

Stable

Mode Collapse

Unstable

Structure
Structure refers to the internal organization or layout of something.

Discontinuous

Continuous

Smooth

Random Empty Regions

KL Divergence

Spectral Normalization

GANs

MSE

Sequence modeling involves modeling sequences of events or data, as seen in text generation.

Autoregressive language formulation is a technique used in text generation models.

Long Short-Term Memory
Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is a type of neural network architecture used for sequence modeling.

LSTM
LSTM is a method used for sequence modeling in text generation.

Text Generation with Generative AI
This is the main topic of the text, which is on text generation with generative AI.

Long Short-Term Memory Networks
LSTM networks are discussed as a solution to the vanishing gradient problem in recurrent neural networks.

LSTM Networks
LSTM networks are specifically mentioned as addressing the vanishing gradient problem in text generation.

LSTM Cell
The LSTM cell is described as a component within LSTM networks used for sequence modeling in text generation.

Forget Gate
The Forget gate is a component of the LSTM cell architecture used for text generation.

Input Gate
The Input gate is a component of the LSTM cell architecture used for text generation.

Candidate Cell Update
The Candidate Cell Update is a component of the LSTM cell architecture used for text generation.

Cell State Update
The Cell State Update is a component of the LSTM cell architecture used for text generation.

Output Gate
The Output gate is a component of the LSTM cell architecture used for text generation.

Transformer
Transformers are described as a type of model used for text generation.

Transformer Decoder
The Transformer decoder is a component used in the Transformer-based text generation model.

Scaled Dot-Product Self-Attention
Scaled dot-product self-attention is a component of the Transformer decoder used in text generation.

Self-Attention Maps
Self-attention maps (Q, K, V) are derived from input matrix X.

Scaling Factor
The scaling factor (√d) is used to prevent gradient saturation in high-dimensional inner products.

Causal Attention Mask
A causal attention mask (M) is applied to hide future tokens in text generation.

Multi-Head Attention
Multi-Head Attention (MHA) allows joint attention to different representation subspaces.

Positional Encoding
Positional encoding is used to inject sequence order into the input embeddings.

Fine-Tuning Language Models
Fine-tuning language models involves adapting them for specific downstream tasks.

Supervised Fine-Tuning
Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) trains a model on structured instruction-response pairs.

Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT / LoRA) uses Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to update only trainable matrices.

Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) involves a learned reward model and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO).

Direct Preference Optimization
Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) directly optimizes the model using preference pairs.

𝑥

𝛽log
𝛽log is a logarithmic term in generative models.

100m Sprint Record
A 100-meter sprint record was broken during the World Athletics Championship.

Carbon-Fiber Spikes
Carbon-fiber spikes are advanced sprinting shoes.

World Athletics Federation
The World Athletics Federation is the governing body of the World Athletics Championship.

Greedy Decoding
Greedy Decoding selects the most probable next token at each step.

Beam Search
Beam Search maintains multiple high-probability sequences at each step.

Top-𝐾 Sampling
Top-𝐾 Sampling retains only the top 𝐾 most probable tokens.

Top-𝑃 (Nucleus) Sampling
Top-𝑃 (Nucleus) Sampling retains only the smallest subset of tokens whose cumulative probability mass exceeds a threshold.

Text Decoding Strategies & Sampling Techniques
These are methods used in text generation to optimize and diversify the output.

Text Decoding Strategies
These are techniques used to improve the quality and diversity of text generation.

Text Generation Applications & Evaluation Metrics
These are categories for categorizing applications and metrics used in evaluating text generation models.

Evaluation Metrics
Metrics such as Perplexity, BLEU, and ROUGE are used to evaluate text generation models.

BLEU Score
BLEU Score measures the precision of 𝑛-grams in machine translation.

ROUGE Score
ROUGE Score measures the recall-focused 𝑛-gram and longest common subsequence overlap in summarization.

Perplexity
Perplexity measures the average cross-entropy per token, which is a measure of model language quality.

Real Time Performance Inputs
Inputs for real-time enhancement of human performance in accompaniment and production.

Transfer Learning
Transfer learning enables models to leverage representations from large musical corpora for adaptation to smaller target domains.

Large Multi-Instrument Multi-Genre Symbolic Data
Large multi-instrument, multi-genre symbolic data serves as the pre-training corpus for music composition laws.

Pre-Training Domain
Learning general music composition laws, such as rhythm, voice leading, chord progressions, and octave relationships, on large corpora.

Feature Extraction
Feature extraction technique where pre-trained network layers are frozen and a new classifier/generator is trained on target domain data.

Fine-Tuning
Fine-tuning involves updating all network weights or a head classifier/generator on target domain data with a small learning rate to prevent catastrophic forgetting.

Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)
Low-rank adaptation technique where rank decomposition matrices are injected into pre-trained weight matrices.

Adapters
Adapters are small trainable feed-forward layers inserted inside Transformer attention or feed-forward blocks to keep main parameters frozen.

Conditional Prompting & Attribute Tokens
Conditional prompting involves prepending control tokens to the tokenized sequence during training and fine-tuning to specify specific attributes like tempo, instrumentation, key signature, and genre identity.

Controllable Latent Spaces
Model latent spaces designed to disentangle various musical attributes and allow independent manipulation.

Loss Weighting & Stylistic Regularization
Loss weighting and stylistic regularization techniques include adding penalty terms to the negative log-likelihood loss to ensure adherence to genre-specific rules.

Copyright & Training Data Ownership
Training models on protected musical works without explicit licenses raises concerns about copyright infringement and fair use.

Vocal Cloning & Right of Publicity
Synthesizing recognizable vocal timbres from real artists poses ethical risks regarding consent and misrepresentation.

Attribution, Watermarking & Watermark Detection
Embedding imperceptible watermarks in generated music files to ensure provenance and prevent deceptive uploads.

Cultural Diversity vs. Bias
Dominant training sets in AI-generated music tend to favor Western traditions, limiting native support for microtonal systems.

Core Concepts
Transfer learning is a technique that leverages pre-training and fine-tuning approaches to adapt generative models to specific domains.

human performance
Real-time inputs are used to enhance human performance during accompaniment and production.

model latent spaces
Controllable latent spaces enable the manipulation of musical attributes like melody, harmony, rhythm, timbre, and dynamics.

Advanced Techniques
Transfer learning is a core concept evolving into advanced techniques such as real-time audio synthesis and neural audio codecs.

Emerging Trends
Transfer learning is a technique that is developing into emerging trends like real-time interactive co-creation and latent spaces for music synthesis.

Ethical Considerations
Transfer learning introduces challenges like copyright infringement, vocal cloning risks, and bias in cultural diversity.

Future Directions
Ethical considerations are intertwined with the evolution of future AI-driven music generation technologies.

Technological Evolution
Ethical considerations drive the evolution of AI-driven music generation, leading to paradigm shifts in methodologies and techniques.

UNIT-IV
UNIT-IV focuses on Music Generation using Generative AI.

Music Generation
Music generation involves capturing temporal dynamics, harmonic structures, and polyphonic dependencies.

MIDI
MIDI represents musical events symbolically and records them as discrete sequences.

Piano Roll Representation
Piano Roll Representation visualizes music as a 2D binary matrix with time steps and pitch dimensions.

LSTM-Based Music Generation
LSTMs process music as temporal sequences by maintaining a persistent cell state for learning long-term patterns.

Transformer-Based Music Generation
Transformer architectures process long sequences in parallel to capture multi-bar themes and harmonic structures.

Causal Transformer Architecture
Causal Transformer Architecture maintains an autoregressive generation pipeline by using causal self-attention.

MuseGAN
MuseGAN is a method for generating polyphonic music compositions.

MIDI Dataset
The Lakh MIDI Dataset is used for training MuseGAN.

Symbolic Music Datasets
Symbolic Music Datasets are converted into multi-track piano-roll tensors for training.

Sigmoid
Sigmoid is used as an activation function in generating layers of MuseGAN.

Wasserstein GAN
Wasserstein GAN is used to optimize the training of multi-track GANs.

Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP)
Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) is used to handle training instability in multi-track GANs.

3D Transposed Convolutions
3D Transposed Convolutions are used to expand temporal dimensions for multi-bar generation.

Polyphonic Music Datasets
Polyphonic Music Datasets are used for training MuseGAN.

Lakh MIDI Dataset
The Lakh MIDI Dataset is a specific polyphonic music dataset used for training MuseGAN.

Positional Encodings
Positional encodings are used to inject structural relationships based on the distance between notes, preserving musical motifs.

Standard Absolute Positional Encodings
Standard absolute positional encodings struggle with musical concepts such as key transpositions or repeating rhythm motifs.

Relative Positional Encodings
Relative Positional Encodings are a modification of standard encodings that maintain musical motifs regardless of their position in a piece.

Pitch Class Histogram Distance
Measures KL divergence between the distribution of 12 chromatic pitch classes in generated music and a target dataset.

Scale Consistency
Calculates the ratio of generated notes that fit within a dominant musical scale (e.g., C Major).

Empty Bar Rate (EBR)
Measures the percentage of generated bars that contain no active note events.

Polyphonic Density
Calculates the average number of simultaneous active notes per bar or beat.

Perplexity (PPL)
Measures how well an autoregressive model predicts unseen test MIDI event sequences.

Binary Thresholding & Binarization
Binary Thresholding and Binarization strategies are applied during inference to form discrete binary notes.

Multi-Bar Generation
3D Transposed Convolutions are used to expand the temporal dimensions for multi-bar generation.

Human-in-the-Loop Interaction
Composers can fix specific instrument tracks and use MuseGAN's discriminator/generator for human-in-the-loop synthesis.

Track Interdependence
Composers can tune the ratio between shared and track-private noise to control inter-track dynamics.

Hybrid Model
The Hybrid model combines shared inter-track noise with track-private noise.

Target Property
Measures the similarity between the distribution of 12 chromatic pitch classes in generated music and a target dataset.

Temporal Model
The Temporal Model extends the Hybrid model by adding temporal latent variables for multi-bar rhythmic and thematic continuity.
